fichas.title: Repair of timber-framed external walls
fichas.summary: Repair guidance for timber-framed walls emphasizes preserving and repairing original loam infill, keeping infill non-load-bearing, and using constructional timber protection. The diagrams compare infill materials and repair build-ups, including externally insulated and internally clad options. Brick infill can stiffen the frame, while lightweight infill lacks thermal storage capacity.
uses: Upgrade walls for current energy and structural requirements

fichas.title: Repair and thermal improvement of natural stone façades
fichas.summary: The page describes improving the energy performance of solid walls with natural stone or stucco façades, often through internal insulation. Where stone cladding is replaced, insulation may be placed behind it, with stone panels fixed to an independent support structure while preserving the façade outline and proportions. External insulation must also be checked for boundary or building-line impacts.
fichas.building_type: Buildings with natural stone or stucco façades
uses: Improve thermal performance while preserving façade character
Assess external insulation projection against boundaries and building lines

fichas.title: Maximum heat transmission coefficients for building elements
fichas.summary: A table gives maximum heat transmission coefficients for new installation, replacement, or conversion of building elements in existing buildings under EnEV 2009. Values are differentiated by building-zone temperature categories. The table covers external walls, ceilings and roofs, flat roofs, elements adjoining unheated rooms or earth, floor construction, and slabs with outside air below.
spaces: Zones adjoining unheated rooms or earth
uses: Check maximum heat transmission coefficients for building work
Guide insulation upgrades and element replacement
